subject.title: Workboard worktree dispatch bypasses the operator.admin gate on arbitrary-repo worktree creation (confused deputy)

question: How should OpenClaw handle this public Workboard worktree authorization bypass before a fix is staged?
rationale: The source-backed issue crosses an operator scope boundary and can expose .worktreeinclude-selected ignored files, while SECURITY.md prefers private handling for unpatched vulnerability details; automation should not choose disclosure or mitigation policy on its own.

options.title: Route through security and patch
options.body: Move triage into the security handling path, then land a focused fix that prevents write-only cards from carrying unvalidated arbitrary repo roots into later admin dispatch.

options.title: Patch publicly in this issue
options.body: Keep discussion public and land a narrow fix here, accepting that the exploit path remains visible until release.

options.title: Close as out of scope
options.body: Treat write-scoped Gateway clients as fully trusted operators and close without code change, despite the current operator.admin contracts for explicit host paths.

recommendation.title: Route through security and patch
recommendation.body: Move triage into the security handling path, then land a focused fix that prevents write-only cards from carrying unvalidated arbitrary repo roots into later admin dispatch.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant Workboard/worktree code and docs were introduced by steipete, and the choice is a security boundary policy decision for that surface.
